metadata.title: The second Bougard-Joret line to order 24: an exhaustive check, the extremal graphs at 35 triples, and a construction without a clique partition for every odd alpha
metadata.description:
Let f(n, α, k) be the least number of edges of a k-connected graph with n vertices and independence number α. Bougard and Joret conjectured f(n, α, k) = t(n, α) + ⌈kα/2⌉ for n > kα, where t(n, α) counts the edges of α disjoint balanced cliques; Didin has announced a proof of the lower bound. We give an independent exhaustive check.

At every one of the 53 triples with α ≥ 3, k ≥ 3 and n ≤ 24 outside the range that Bougard and Joret's Proposition 8 settles, f equals the conjectured value, by enumerating 6,223,452,780 candidate graphs with nauty's generator, an independence prune proved sound and an exact filter; for seven pairs (α, k) this settles the conjectured value for every n > kα. A validation suite tests every component against an independent implementation, known counts and byte-identical rebuilds.

We list all 246 extremal graphs at 35 triples: those that split into α cliques have Bougard and Joret's structure, and the other 40, all with k = 3 and α odd, do not. Two blocks recovered from them give, for every odd α and 3α < n ≤ 4α − 1, a 3-connected graph of the conjectured size with independence number α and no partition into α cliques. Conditional on Didin's main theorem and for α ≥ 3, these graphs and eight graphs at (10, 3, 3) are all the extremal graphs without such a partition, by a reduction to blocks on at most seven vertices and an exhaustive check.

Source code, data and computational records: https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CAOS_RESEARCH (problems/combinatorics/bougard-joret/experiments, EXP-005 to EXP-014).
metadata.version_notes: Adds the characterisation of the extremal graphs without a partition into alpha cliques for alpha >= 3, conditional on Didin's main theorem (Theorem 3 of Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.22831382): a reduction to blocks on at most seven vertices and an exhaustive check of all graphs on five to seven vertices (EXP-014) leave only the blocks X6 and X7 at the attaching triples observed in the data, so these constructions and eight graphs at (10,3,3) are all such extremal graphs; alpha >= 3 is needed (an extremal graph at (7,2,3) has no partition into two cliques). Also: f = t + ceil(k alpha / 2) derived from Didin's Theorem 3 alone; sections for the experimental design, the ablation of the prune and the limitations; the growth factor reported with its standard deviation; the abstract shortened to 226 printed words (v0.03 printed about 270).
